  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Structural graph decomposition}

---

```{r}
library(gAtoms)
g <- igraph::make_ring(6, circular = FALSE)
g <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(g, "name", value = letters[1:6])
dec <- atom_decompose(g)
dec
atoms(dec)
separators(dec)
prime_ordering(dec)
validate(dec, expensive = TRUE)
```

Each connected component has an alternating sequence
\(P_1,S_2,P_2,\ldots,S_k,P_k\). Each separator is the current atom's intersection
with its earlier tree parent, and with the union of earlier atoms. The order is
constructed by deterministic leaf peeling after the native atom tree is complete.
Raw RDA separators remain available in the expert `decompose_atoms()` result;
they are not indexed by the final ordering.

```{r}
stats::residuals(dec)
dec$parent
dec$children
dec$complete
summary(dec)
plot(dec)
```

The native backend uses zero-based IDs. Public sets preserve names, or contain
one-based indices when no names are supplied. `vertex_map` records both. Sparse
adjacency inputs stay sparse throughout normalization and decomposition.

```{r}
sparse <- as_dgCMatrix(dec)
as_igraph(sparse)
disconnected <- igraph::disjoint_union(g, igraph::make_empty_graph(1, directed = FALSE))
# Assign unique labels after combining independently named/unnamed graphs.
disconnected <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(disconnected, "name", value = letters[1:7])
forest <- atom_decompose(disconnected)
forest$component_orderings
validate(forest)
```

No edges or empty separators connect unrelated components. An isolated vertex
has one atom and an ordering of length one. This structural API supports later
statistical modules but does not implement them.
